_comment: FIX (reproducibility, review item #9). Copy this file per optimizer run and fill it in — the notebooks write one of these automatically next to each candidate's exported instructions. Foundry's optimizer is a hosted, versioned, non-deterministic service; without this record a 'Run 1 vs Run 2' comparison cannot be attributed cleanly to optimizer search stochasticity vs. silent model-version drift vs. eval-time sampling noise.

outputs.composite_score_note: This is the Optimize wizard's own reported number, computed in-sample against dataset.file_uploaded (dataset/optimize.jsonl). It is NOT a holdout score and compare_to_foundry.py never treats it as one.
outputs.holdout_composite_score_note: Leave null until a response-level harness runs this exported candidate against dataset/holdout.jsonl and scores its real responses/tool calls with the shared score_response function (see _baselines/dspy_mipro/metric.py). That harness does not exist in this pack yet (docs/paper/paper-v4.md Sec 5.2/8) -- compare_to_foundry.py reports the gap explicitly rather than substituting composite_score.
outputs.cost_estimate_note: Fill baseline/optimized_est_cost_per_call_usd from _tools/model_pricing.estimate_cost_usd(input_tokens, output_tokens, eval_model.name) against this candidate's real instruction word count and mean holdout response word count, the same word-count-proxy token estimate _baselines/dspy_mipro/run_mipro_baseline.py uses for the DSPy track, so the two tracks' cost-growth-ratio numbers (paper-v4.md Table 7) are computed the same way. Leave null (never 0) if eval_model.name isn't in PRICE_TABLE.
